experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count: the first 14 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages. One birthday search per organizer trial over fresh inputs from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: A search of at most 1200 fresh inputs returns a pair whose digests agree on those 14 bits in every trial, as a random 14-bit function would. Checks the digest of the selected target at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count, on the line construction of proof.md section 2: the first 6 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages that are the antipodal points W = c+s and W = c-s about a centre c of the line j = 0 of the first two rounds. One scan of the pairs s = 1, ..., 150 per organizer trial, the centre from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: The digest difference F(c+s) - F(c-s) = 2 s g_c(s^2) of the antipodal points behaves as a random function of s at width 6: a trial returns a pair with probability 1-(1-2^-6)^150 = 0.9058, about 232 of the 256 trials. Checks the digest of the selected target on the antipodal line pairs of the attack at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Euclidean normality of the attack's own construction at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.5, 10.5.1). For two centres c per trial (the first from the trial seed, the second from the seed and its index) the program builds F_2(c + X), the coordinate 0 after the first 2 S-box layers on the line j = 0 of the first two rounds (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part g about c (degree m = 12), R = X^((p-1)/2) mod g and the complete Euclidean remainder sequence of (g, R - 1), exactly over F_p. Trials 0-255 are computed, 512 sequences (seed set a, entry 1 of 2). A trial whose two sequences are both normal (deg(R - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient of degree 1 down to the gcd) returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits, found among 65 line points (certain, by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal, so exactly 256 of the 256 trials return a pair. If sequences were abnormal at the rate 0.003 (the allowance delta of H-NORMAL, proof.md 9.5), all 512 would be normal with probability 0.215, and all 1,024 of the two entries euclid-normal-n2-t256-l2-a and -b with probability 0.046. Per computed trial the program reports the untrusted observations sequences, normal_sequences, selfcheck_ok, abnormal_quotients, gcd_positive (about 2 of 5 centres) and max_quotient_degree. Supports H-NORMAL at m = 12 on the construction's own pairs; it says nothing about the scale m of the claim, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: One trial of the attack algorithm at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.1, 9.5, 10.5.1). For a centre c from the trial seed the program builds F_2(c + X) (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part g (degree m = 12), R = X^((p-1)/2) mod g and the complete Euclidean sequence of (g, R - 1) with its gcd G, exactly over F_p; deg G = k(c), the number of usable roots. If the sequence is normal and 1 <= k(c) <= 16, it isolates a root S of G (stage E, shifts from the seed), takes s = sqrt(S) and checks F_2(c + s) = F_2(c - s) by direct evaluation. Trials 0-255 are computed. A trial that passes returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits (65 line points, certain by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. The checked pair count is the number of centres where one trial at depth 2 succeeds.
experiments.hypothesis: Every sequence is normal (H-NORMAL) and 1 <= k(c) <= 16 has probability 0.393469 at m = 12 (proof.md 9.3: the law of the positive fixed points of the signed permutation group B_m, the monodromy computed at this depth in 10.3; Poisson(1/2) gives 1 - e^(-1/2) = 0.393469), so the pair count is Binomial(256, 0.393469): mean 100.7, standard deviation 7.8, two-sigma range 86 to 116 (three-sigma 78 to 124). Per computed trial the program reports the untrusted observations n_layers, m, gcd_degree, normal, abnormal_quotients, selfcheck, iso_rounds, root_check and witness_points. Supports the premises H-ONE and H-NORMAL at m = 12 on the construction's own polynomial; it says nothing about the scale m of the claim, where they are extrapolated.
